discovery.none: Deliberate. Other brands' serial modules are generic, and no discriminating advertisement name is established. Ninebot Z shares its Nordic-UART service/characteristic trio with Ninebot/Segway scooters, InMotion V2 and unrelated UART peripherals; it also shares the 5A A5 outer framing with the scooter. Neither is an advertisement matcher. Require manual model selection and post-connect role-address/payload confirmation before any GATT write. Do not route a bare NUS fingerprint to this spec or to ninebot-segway-ble.yaml.

device.name: Electric Unicycles (King Song / Gotway-Begode / Veteran / Ninebot Z) — WheelLog
device.notes:
Electric unicycles from King Song, Gotway/Begode, Veteran/Leaperkim and Ninebot Z are decoded by the open-source WheelLog Android app. Each brand uses framed packets over a BLE serial notify stream; brand is identified from the first packets rather than a fixed advertised UUID. Fully local BLE, no cloud. The per-brand frame formats below are the load-bearing facts. Other brands' transport UUIDs are device-specific; Ninebot Z's reported Nordic-UART trio is declared below without making it a matcher.
KING SONG (KingsongAdapter): 20-byte frame, header AA 55, trailer 14 5A 5A; the packet-type selector is byte 16. Live-data type 0xA9: voltage bytes 2-3 (LE), speed 4-5, total distance 6-9 (32-bit), current 10-11, temperature 12-13. Other types: 0xB9 distance/time/fan, 0xBB name/model, 0xB3 serial, 0xA4/0xB5 speed/alarm settings, 0xF1/0xF2 dual-battery BMS. Commands (write byte 16): beep 0x88, request name 0x9B, request serial 0x63, power-off 0x40.
GOTWAY / BEGODE (GotwayAdapter): 24-byte frame, header 55 AA, footer 5A 5A 5A 5A (bytes 20-23); type byte at index 18 — 0x00 live "Frame A", 0x04 "Frame B" (totals/settings), 0x07 motor-temp/batt-current, 0x01/0x02/0x03 BMS, 0xFF advanced settings. Frame A (big-endian): voltage 2-3 (1/100 V), speed 4-5 (km/h = x3.6), distance 8-9 (m), phase current 10-11 (1/100 A signed), temperature 12-13 (v/340 + 36.53 C), PWM 14-15. Voltage base 67.2 V with a config-selected multiplier (0->1.0x ... 4->2.0x) to cover 84/100.8 V packs. Commands (ASCII): beep 'b', calibration 'c', lights E/Q/T, max-speed 'W', miles/km 'm'/'g'.
VETERAN / LEAPERKIM (VeteranAdapter): header DC 5A 5C + length byte; big-endian: voltage @4, speed @6 (x10 signed), distance @8 (word-reversed int), total distance @12, phase current @16 (x10), temperature @18; CRC32 on longer frames. 24S (100.8 V nominal) reference.
NINEBOT Z (NinebotZAdapter): variable-length 5A A5 frames with a clear payload-length byte, a 16-bit ones-complement checksum and repeating-XOR obfuscation keyed by a 16-byte session value. Controller and dual-BMS read-only identification/telemetry are in protocol_details.euc_frame_formats.ninebot_z. This is not the scooter register protocol in ninebot-segway-ble.yaml.
SAFETY: beep/lights/max-speed/calibration commands are unauthenticated by design in these decoders. The Ninebot Z variant added here declares no vehicle settings, calibration, power or speed writes.

openness.notes: No vendor documentation; WheelLog reverse-engineered each brand's frames. Other brands' serial UUIDs remain module-specific. The Ninebot Z NUS trio is restated from the cited constants and GATT fingerprints only as a reported post-connect transport.

credentials.notes: No pairing/auth documented; frames are unauthenticated over BLE. No Wi-Fi.
stored_on_device: Per-brand wheel settings (speed limits, alarms, lights)

factory_reset.effect: No documented BLE factory reset; per-brand settings are command writes, not a single reset. Not transcribed here.

methods.description: Manually select the exact wheel before any GATT write. Connect over BLE, subscribe to the wheel's serial/notify characteristic, and decode incoming frames per the selected brand. For Ninebot Z, use only the documented read requests and confirm role addresses and payloads; never treat NUS or the shared outer frame as model confirmation.

steps.action: Manually select the exact wheel model; for a Ninebot Z, do not rely on NUS or the shared 5A A5/L+9 outer frame for identity.
Connect and subscribe to the selected wheel's BLE serial characteristic, without writing yet.
After manual model confirmation, use only the selected brand's documented read requests; for a Ninebot Z, confirm its role addresses and payload layouts and stop on a scooter register reply.

setup.notes: Connect to the wheel's BLE serial characteristic and subscribe to notifications; the brand is auto-detected from the first packets. No pairing secret. Confidence medium: King Song and Gotway frames are fully read from the adapters; Veteran offsets are read but less cross-checked. Ninebot Z's NUS trio is reported transport, not identity. Its real key installation remains pending capture; see protocol_details.euc_frame_formats.ninebot_z.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new BLE client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The per-brand frame formats (headers, field offsets, command bytes) are from WheelLog's Android per-brand adapters; Ninebot Z also uses its upstream unit tests as reported evidence. Other brands' serial UUIDs remain module-specific and unasserted. The Ninebot Z Nordic-UART trio is reported by WheelLog's constants and GATT fingerprints, but is transport only and never identity.

variants.notes: Distinct WheelLog wire variant, selected manually and confirmed only by its post-connect role addresses and payload layouts. Its NUS trio and 5A A5 header are shared with the scooter spec and are not identity.

evidence.open_questions: The real key-response selector, key installation and connection-state sequence remain pending capture. Parameter 0x00 is only a decoder branch; parameter 0x01 is observed but unhandled. The advertised-name identity is not established. Operating-time seconds and BMS capacity units come from the decoder's semantics, not a new capture.
evidence.open_source_review: Ninebot Z framing, address and command constants, repeating-XOR transform, telemetry and BMS layouts were transcribed from WheelLog's open-source NinebotZAdapter.java at 1b3707973e3b4528bd88778f9ebdf7a79817cf3f. The reported NUS trio comes from Constants.kt and Ninebot Z entries in bluetooth_services.json, not from an advertisement capture. The decoder's key-installation branch accepts parameter 0x00; the sole upstream key sample instead carries parameter 0x01 and is unhandled. Synthetic vectors here prove only the codec with invented identifiers, never negotiation. All are reported and untested against hardware by this project.

checksum.algorithm: ones-complement of the unsigned byte sum, modulo 16 bits
checksum.coverage: Length through the final payload byte, before obfuscation; excludes the 5A A5 header and the checksum itself.
checksum.invalid: Reject the frame; do not parse its payload.

length.counts: Payload bytes only, excluding header, length, source, destination, command, parameter and checksum.

obfuscation.formula: For body index i >= 1, transformed[i] = plaintext[i] XOR session_key[(i - 1) mod 16]. The same operation decodes and encodes.
obfuscation.scope: Apply to the complete body after 5A A5, including the checksum, but leave body byte 0 (payload_length) unchanged.
obfuscation.security: Obfuscation only, not authentication or a secure session.

plaintext_body.description: The bytes after 5A A5 after repeating-XOR decoding. Offsets below are relative to the length byte, not the frame header.

reassembly: Accumulate the notification byte stream; a frame may start or end in any BLE notification and several frames may share one notification.
Scan for 5A A5, then read the clear payload_length byte. Wait for exactly payload_length + 9 bytes from the first 5A byte.
A 5A A5 sequence inside a collecting frame is payload, not a new header. Decode and checksum only after the declared frame length is present.
After a complete or invalid frame, resume scanning after it (or after the rejected header) so noise and fragmented headers do not permanently wedge the parser.

bms_cells.cell_count_rule: Start at 14 cells. If cell 15 (offset 28) is nonzero use 15; if cell 16 (offset 30) is nonzero use 16. Zero-valued trailing cells are absent.

parse_rules: Bytes 0-13: 14-byte ASCII BMS serial; test serials are invented.
Version: hexadecimal byte 15, then the high nibble of byte 14, then the low nibble of byte 14, joined with dots (for bytes 23 01, version 1.2.3).
Manufacture date: raw = uint16 LE at 32; year = 2000 + (raw >> 9), month = (raw >> 5) & 0x0f, day = raw & 0x1f.
Bytes 20-21 and 26-31 are not interpreted by the source.

controller_serial.encoding: ASCII serial number, exactly 14 bytes in the source examples; the vectors use an invented serial.

fields.notes: Read as operating time by the source but not consumed there; seconds are reported, not hardware-confirmed.

read_requests.request_payload_meaning: For ordinary reads, the one-byte request payload is the requested response payload length in bytes. The request's own payload_length is therefore 1; the empty key request has length 0.

ninebot_z.scope: Read-only identification and telemetry for the Ninebot Z electric unicycle. This is a distinct WheelLog variant, not the Ninebot/Segway scooter register protocol in ninebot-segway-ble.yaml. They share the 5A A5 header, clear length and L+9/checksum outer framing; the Z is distinguished by repeating-XOR, role addresses and payload layouts. No vehicle setting, calibration, power, light, lock, alarm, speed-limit or firmware write is declared.

decoder_accepted_key_branch.behavior: When this branch matches, the decoder copies the payload into its 16-byte transform key. This source-code branch is not evidence that a real key reply uses parameter 0x00.

session.notes: The source implements read-only requests and starts its transform key at 16 zero bytes. Its timer transitions and sole key sample do not establish a negotiation sequence or a working key installation. Parameter 0x00 is only the decoder-accepted branch; parameter 0x01 is observed but unhandled. Capture is required before relying on either.

observed_unhandled_key_reply.evidence: The sole key-reply sample in NinebotZAdapterTest.kt.
observed_unhandled_key_reply.handling: Does not match the decoder's parameter-0x00 key branch, so the cited decoder does not install this sample as a key.

ninebot_z.source: WheelLog NinebotZAdapter.java, Constants.kt, bluetooth_services.json and NinebotZAdapterTest.kt at 1b3707973e3b4528bd88778f9ebdf7a79817cf3f; no hardware replay by this project.
ninebot_z.test_vectors_description: Synthetic codec-only vectors independently generated from the declared transform. The 16-byte transform key and every controller/BMS serial are invented; protocol role addresses are constants, not host Bluetooth addresses. These vectors prove framing, checksum, XOR and layout implementation only, never key negotiation or installation.

transport.evidence: WheelLog Constants.kt and Ninebot Z entries in bluetooth_services.json.
transport.notes: Shared with the scooter and other NUS peripherals. Declare only as post-connect transport. Manual model selection and Z role/payload confirmation are required before any write; NUS alone never selects this spec or the scooter spec.

remaining_unknowns: Ninebot Z advertised name and whether all units require the session-key exchange; the NUS trio is reported transport, not identity.
The real Ninebot Z key response and installation: parameter 0x00 is only the decoder-accepted branch, while the sole upstream sample is parameter 0x01 and unhandled.
Ninebot Z operating-time units and BMS capacity units on hardware; all protocol details remain reported/untested.
